ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.37912v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Utterance-level similarity ratings do not reveal where perceived accent differences occur in generated speech. We introduce a segmental evaluation protocol combining speaker and accent similarity ratings with subword annotations of perceived accent differences provided by listeners from target accent regions. Using newly collected recordings, 47 retained listeners evaluate 200 content-matched reference--candidate pairs spanning four Scottish and Australian voices, two zero-shot TTS systems, and an articulation-based voice conversion system. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: ODAQ-Collection: Expanding the Open Dataset of Audio Quality with a Focus on Spatial Distortions
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.37959v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Open Dataset of Audio Quality (ODAQ) is an expanding resource that addresses the scarcity of openly available data in audio quality assessment research. While previous contributions focused mainly on timbral distortions, with spatial processing limited to basic mid-side and left-right stereo conditions, we present a new contribution featuring high-quality music and speech recordings with diverse stereo images, controlled spatial distortions, and subjective listening test results from trained listeners in a laboratory setting. With 148 pairs

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Improving the Dependency on Fine-Tuning Data in Transfer Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38050v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compensating for train-test mismatches in acoustic environments is important for deployable speech solutions. This paper proposes to reduce the amount of fine-tuning data needed in transfer learning to mitigate the train-test mismatch by using a compensation mechanism based on the feature maximum likelihood linear regression (fMLLR) algorithm. Our scheme incorporates an autoencoder to reduce the number of trainable parameters. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38252v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. It introduces neural audio codecs and autoencoders, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization in a shared notation. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38316v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern discrete neural audio codecs facilitate speech synthesis by replacing continuous acoustic representations with low-frame-rate discrete token sequences. For Malay speech synthesis, character-level input reduces reliance on pronunciation lexicons. However, combining character-level inputs with low-frame-rate discrete codecs introduces a temporal alignment challenge. When predicted character durations are quantized into frame counts at 12.5 Hz, durations shorter than one codec frame may be assigned zero frames. Consequently, the correspondin

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: MiDiff: MIDI-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Drum Audio Enhancement
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38619v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Bridging the semantic gap between perfect symbolic musical structure and severely degraded acoustic signals offers a powerful paradigm for high-fidelity audio restoration. We introduce MiDiff, a diffusion-based generative model for drum audio enhancement that conditions the reverse process on temporally aligned Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) piano rolls. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: SelectSep: Target-Selective Video Queries for Audio Source Separation
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38624v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video-queried sound separation (VQSS) aims to isolate a target sound from an audio mixture using its corresponding video as a query. However, scene-level video queries can become ambiguous when multiple sounding objects are visible, particularly when the target and interferer are semantically similar. We propose SelectSep, a target-selective VQSS framework that jointly uses text and a single click coordinate to specify the target source and instance without requiring segmentation at inference time. We adapt the visual encoder through target-feat

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Wav2Aug: A Drop-In Speech Augmentation Policy
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38656v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: SpecAugment is the dominant speech augmentation policy, but researchers have studied it primarily for automatic speech recognition (ASR), and it operates on spectrograms, limiting its applicability to other speech tasks and waveform models. We propose Wav2Aug, a drop-in waveform augmentation policy that randomly samples two augmentations from a calibrated pool of waveform transformations. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Personalising Parametric Audio Effect Recommendation for Vocals from Parameter-only Style Priors
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38696v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio effect recommendation has mostly modelled style through reference audio and audio-domain losses. Because the parameter-to-audio map of parametric effects is many-to-one, such systems can match a reference without reflecting how a given engineer works. We instead model an engineer's style as a distribution over effect-chain parameters, which matches the data engineers can realistically share: console recalls store parameters without the audio they were applied to. Under a label-shift assumption, a personalised recommendation follows in clos

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Streaming Speech Recognition on a Microcontroller: a 65.7M-Parameter Transducer in 2 and 4 Bits on the ESP32-P4
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We run Kroko, a 65.7M-parameter streaming Zipformer2 transducer for English, on the ESP32-P4, a microcontroller with two 400 MHz RISC-V cores, a 128-bit SIMD extension (PIE) and 32 MB of PSRAM, but no neural accelerator. Without any training, the encoder's 290 matrices are stored with 2 or 4 bits per weight in Hadamard-rotated groups: the width of each matrix comes from its measured sensitivity, and each matrix is first corrected toward the original model's output, then rounded with GPTQ and a search over the group norms. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Structured Pruning of Feedback Delay Networks
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.38768v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) are recursive filter structures used to synthesise artificial reverberation. Their feedback matrix governs both energy exchange between delay lines and the computation required at every sample, making its design central to balancing an FDN's acoustic performance and implementation efficiency. In this work, we develop an FDN-specific structured pruning method that connects these acoustic and computational concerns, allowing high-order dense orthogonal designs to be fitted to efficient implementations. The feedback m

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Array-Agnostic High-Order Ambisonics Encoding via Diffusion Posterior Sampling
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.39185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambisonics provides a device-independent representation of three-dimensional sound fields; however, extracting these coefficients from practical microphone array recordings remains strongly dependent on array geometry, acoustic transfer functions, and spatial sampling resolution. This pipeline is typically divided into two distinct tasks: encoding, which entails reconstructing the physically resolvable spatial components, and upscaling, which requires generating higher-order coefficients. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Conformal Prediction-Aware DOA Tracking
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.39566v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce an uncertainty-aware DOA-tracking framework combining deep posterior estimation, conformal-prediction calibration, and temporal smoothing. The approach enhances stability against reverberation and burst-like directional noise, yielding more reliable trajectories and greater robustness than conventional DOA-tracking methods.

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: The Importance of Speech Genre for End-of-Turn Detector Training
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.39742v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-of-turn (EoT) detection has been studied mostly through features, models, and modalities, while the speech genre of the training data has drawn far less attention. We isolate this factor. Using one reproducible annotation pipeline, we build a matched pair of corpora, multi-turn human-human conversational and single-turn human-machine, and train the same streaming ConvLSTM EoT detector on each. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Towards Multilingual End-of-Turn Detection using Frozen Speech Encoders
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2610.39755v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A spoken dialogue system must judge when the user has yielded the floor. This end-of-turn (EoT) detector is normally trained and tuned afresh for each language, which is costly to scale to new languages. We instead build one on a frozen multilingual encoder, training only a small fixed-size head. Using five CALLHOME languages, we investigate three questions. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.38109v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deciding which member of an animal group produced a vocalization and where that vocalization was produced are central to studying social communication but are rarely evaluated with physically verified ground truth. Existing resources either localize sounds without identifying the caller, or recognize individuals from isolated vocalizations without reliance on the 3D candidate geometry. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: MixCards: Evaluating Structured Descriptions of Multi-Source Sound Scenes
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.38276v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio captioning benchmarks typically evaluate a single unstructured free-text description of an audio scene, providing limited insight into how a model fails to understand polyphonic audio. A plausible caption may omit a source, or conflate multiple sources into one, or assign an attribute of one source to another, and conventional captioning evaluation cannot locate these errors. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Automated Parameter Sensitivity Ranking in Audio Synthesis
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.38740v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Software synthesizers expose dozens of coupled controls, many of them redundant or perceptually inert at typical operating points. This paper presents a two-stage, measure-and-validate framework that ranks parameters by their influence on the audio output and then checks that ranking against an independent, variance-based experiment. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Few-shot voice cloning makes it cheap to produce daily Japanese financial commentary with several synthetic speakers, but kanji words with more than one reading, such as the word for "market" (shijo vs. ichiba) or "overall trend" (taisei vs. oze), are still misread. A common quality gate transcribes each synthesized sentence with automatic speech recognition (ASR), converts both the input and the transcript to kana, and regenerates on mismatch. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: A learning-based method of automatic music transcription
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39255v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic Music Transcription (AMT) seeks to convert acoustic music recordings into symbolic musical notation, a process that remains remarkably difficult for polyphonic piano due to concurrent polyphony, harmonic partial interference, expressive timing, and severe pitch activation sparsity. In this paper, we formulate polyphonic piano transcription as a frame-level multi-label classification problem across the standard 88 piano pitches (MIDI notes 21 to 108). ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Lightweight Underwater Acoustic Vessel Classification for Embedded Deployment
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a Raspberry Pi-based underwater vessel classification system for edge deployment under limited connectivity, bandwidth and power in offshore acoustic surveillance. Using ShipsEar, we compare six classifiers on a Raspberry Pi 5 through a complete audio-to-prediction pipeline. We assess classification performance, processing latency, CPU utilisation, memory consumption and monitored power. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: EmpDPO: Enabling Emphasis Control in TTS via Direct Preference Optimization
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Word-level emphasis conveys meaning that text alone cannot express and is therefore essential for a practical text-to-speech (TTS) system. In this work, we study how to add emphasis control post hoc to a pretrained TTS model that has never been trained with emphasis annotations. We present EmpDPO, a simple, efficient, and effective two-stage recipe that adds emphasis control to a multilingual zero-shot diffusion TTS model through supervised fine-tuning followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In engineering, applications of artificial intelligence have so far been largely limited to surrogate models and optimization tasks. Large language models changed this, as they can write software from a task given in words. Placed inside a harness, a system of components that lets it search for information and execute software, such a model becomes an agent that can take over recurring engineering tasks. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39754v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a cascade streaming voice privacy system, consisting of ASR, NLP, and TTS modules. By leveraging recent improvements in all three aspects of speech and language processing, we show that such a system is capable of achieving a result comparable to state-of-the-art offline voice privacy systems, while providing controllable capabilities of content protection beyond voice. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.39898v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents an accessible, distributed approach to higher order ambisonics using a network of low-cost microcontroller-based devices. Leveraging recent advances in embedded computing, networked audio, and precise time synchronization, the system offers an alternative to conventional centralized architectures that typically require expensive multichannel interfaces and high-performance digital signal processing hardware. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.40372v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) models clone a target voice from a short reference clip, commonly referred to as the prompt. In practice, the prompt has to be cut from a longer recording of the speaker, so which part to use must be chosen. To understand what makes a good prompt, we analyze hundreds of thousands of outputs synthesized by four TTS models from candidate prompts of YouTube recordings. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.40414v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep audio classifiers can achieve strong predictive performance, but their hidden representations remain difficult to interpret. Existing audio explainability methods often focus on input-level attribution, such as waveform segments, spectrogram regions, or acoustic features, and provide limited insight into what hidden neurons encode. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2610.37795v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) characterizes the local frequency content of time-varying signals by evaluating the discrete Fourier transform over a sliding analysis window. The STFT is governed by a fundamental resolution trade-off: a short window localizes rapid transients in time at the cost of frequency resolution, whereas a long window resolves closely spaced harmonics at the expense of temporal resolution. CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Cheap handheld gaming consoles now often pack surprising processing power. But many risk ending up as e-waste. A new open-source project is turning them into powerful Linux music workstations, instead, complete with the ability to run plug-ins—and original games, too. Oh, and the project has some familiar faces involved. Here's an exclusive first look.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Inside NI Absynth 6.2 and its updated workflows for exploring sound
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
This month, Absynth got two updates that refine its UI and editing navigation, freeing you up to shape your sound. Product designer Hannah Lockwood and Absynth creator Brian Clevinger join us to talk about the work they did on that. I already knew Hannah and Brian were really passionate about their craft, so let's get our tour from the source -- and dive into more Absynth sonic frontiers.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: On the sublime BETHLEHEM بيت لحم, walls in time and space fall
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
The exquisite collaboration of Lawrence Sammour, Sary Moussa, and Abed Kobeissy, Bethlehem, is released this month. And it has become a rich sanctuary, a shared space that refuses erasure or fragmentation. It also refuses to obey the boundaries of colonialism and occupation, weaving together what was pulled apart, as taut and resonant as the strings of the buzuq.

The post On the sublime BETHLEHEM بيت لحم, walls in time and space fall appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Free Friday: GForce’s superb Axxess instrument is free until December
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
GForce has updated their site, branding, and pricing (now with both lifetime licenses and subscription options). And there are two freebies, time-limited through the end of November: a Mellotron M400 instrument, and the one I suspect most readers will be into, GForce's take on the 1975 ARP Axxe synthesizer.

The post Free Friday: GForce’s superb Axxess instrument is free until December appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Free Friday: D16 is turning 20 and they’ve got a new free stereo delay
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Straight outta Katowice, our friends at D16 Audio Group are celebrating 20 years with an all-new stereo delay: Echolite. And don't let the "lite" in the name deceive you: this all-new giveaway has some power beneath its simple UI.
